text: Understanding databases is an important skill in today's digital world. A database stores information in an organised way. Traditional databases use tables, where each row is a record and each column is a field. We use queries, usually written in SQL, to find and change data. However, not all databases work this way. NoSQL databases store data differently, for example as documents, and they are often more flexible. Good data modelling helps you plan the structure before you build it. Finally, indexes make searches much faster, although they use extra space. Choosing the right type of database depends on your needs.
